I know some people have been wary of making one of these, but I feel it's a good idea. You can't have account management, for example, implemented as part of the site itself. You also can't have saving posts offline implemented as a part of Voat, for obvious reasons. It's stuff like this we should add to an Enhancement Suite. An enhancement suite should not be bloated with features that should be built in to the site itself, but it would be great to have for certain features. I plan on making it, unless it's already being worked on. I've never done anything major with Browser Add-On development, but I do know my way around the Firefox SDK and JavaScript. I think I'll wait to really get started with it until the site is out of Alpha however, so that I know exactly what will need to be done and how it's going to need to be done. I don't want to be extending a site that isn't even finished yet.

I just wanted to put it out there that I think it's necessary and I plan on doing it. I'll welcome help from anyone who wants to give it, and if anyone has any suggestions I'll hear them.

EDIT: I wasn't sure if this was the right subverse for this or if would fit better in /v/voatdev. I decided on here because I feel /v/voatdev is more for development of Voat itself, while this would be a user extension to Voat. Correct me if I'm wrong though.
I want to make a Voat Enhancement Suite
Saving posts seems like the obvious feature, it would also be cool of it loaded up the next page at the bottom, like reddit does. That is the only feature I miss. Thanks for offering to do this!

First off, I liked the Dredd movie, but I've heard so many people say it's better than the Stallone movie because it's "more true to the comics" and I just don't know what they're talking about. It's crazy to me how it portrayed the criminals as dirty scumbags, the civilians as innocent people caught in the middle, and the judges as a superhero underdog police force just trying to make the world a better place. The level of force the judges had was depicted as being an appropriate and necessary response to an out-of-control city which had been taken over by crime.

The Judge Dredd 2000AD comics, on the other hand, were 100% political satire (and, by the way, campy and humorous, not gritty action comics). They served as criticisms of authoritarian governments and police states. Criminals were still basically depicted as dirty scumbags (although not always psychopaths like they literally all are in the movie), but, crucially, innocent civilians were treated like criminals by the judges too, who would often be seen giving out outrageously unfair sentences to random pedestrians (like parking violations for being too fat) while walking between locations. Dredd was the "perfect" cop because he was a complete sociopath. He had zero compassion, and followed the law to the letter - moral justice was irrelevant, only legal justice mattered.

Of course the movie has a bit more nuance than I give it credit for, and there have been lots of incarnations of Dredd in the comics, some of them with more sympathetic depictions of Dredd, but still. It just seems to me like Judge Dredd is more relevant nowadays than ever, with the increasing militarization of US police forces and frequent criticisms of some western countries becoming more like the homogeneous police state depicted in 2000AD. The Dredd movie, while very cool and enjoyable, is such a wasted opportunity to satirize all of that shit. I'd love another Dredd movie, but not a sequel to the Karl Urban depiction - I'd love to see a movie where Dredd is the bad guy and criminals are depicted as humans.
Karl Urban's Dredd shouldn't have been the good guy: In the comics, Judge Dredd was a satirical parody of overpowered police forces, not cop batman
